entities.summary: Jorge Cabral was a Portuguese nobleman and explorer who played a pivotal role in the governance of Portuguese India. Born into a prominent family, Cabral was appointed as the 15th ruler of Portuguese India as governor from 13 June 1549 to November 1550. During his tenure, he oversaw the expansion of Portuguese trade and commerce in the region, establishing strategic alliances with local rulers and securing key territories. Cabral's legacy extends beyond his governance of Portuguese India, as he also contributed to the exploration and mapping of the Indian Ocean. His achievements served as a precursor to the rise of European colonial powers in the region. The impact of Cabral's governance can still be seen in the modern-day cultural and economic landscape of the Indian subcontinent. The Portuguese presence in India, which was significantly expanded during Cabral's tenure, left a lasting legacy in the region's architecture, language, and cuisine. The legacy of Jorge Cabral continues to be studied by historians and scholars today, offering insights into the complexities of colonialism and the evolution of global trade networks.
